game: New England Patriots at Seattle Seahawks

newMaterial.detail: Castro predicts Sam Darnold finishes below 300 passing yards and throws one interception. He notes Darnold averaged 238.1 passing yards per game in 2025, New England allowed only two 300-yard passers, and expects Seattle to be able to lean on its run game and defense if it establishes control.
newMaterial.implication: supports a controlled-volume Seattle passing script and explicit Darnold turnover warning; this is a prediction, not an inferred under-227.5 wager

newMaterial.detail: Castro predicts Arroyo records his first career 50-plus-yard receiving game and scores a touchdown, citing favorable middle-of-field/play-action opportunities if Seattle establishes the run. The article lists Arroyo anytime TD at +1100.
newMaterial.implication: new player-level matchup construction around New England coverage attention and Seattle play action; explicit touchdown prediction retained without inferring stake or conviction

newMaterial.detail: Castro predicts rookie RB Jadarian Price scores his first NFL touchdown, citing Kenneth Walker III's departure and Zach Charbonnet beginning the season on PUP as opening immediate meaningful-touch and goal-line opportunity. The article lists Price anytime TD at +135 and rushing yardage at 51.5.
newMaterial.implication: reinforces Price's immediate goal-line opportunity; no rushing-yardage side is inferred from the listed market

newMaterial.detail: Castro predicts Seattle and New England combine for at least five sacks, citing Seattle's six sacks in Super Bowl LX, Mike Macdonald's pressure packages, New England's own pressure ability and the opportunity to put Drake Maye into obvious passing situations.
newMaterial.implication: adds an explicit high-sack game construction consistent with the pressure-centric matchup mechanism

newMaterial.detail: Castro predicts Seattle 24, New England 20 and says Seattle's defense should again be the largest difference while acknowledging New England is more experienced and Maye should be better prepared for Seattle's schemes.
newMaterial.implication: explicit Seattle straight-up outcome and 44-point score projection; no ATS or total wager is inferred even though the article separately lists Seattle -3.5 and total 44.5
